author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Meredith marked the 25th anniversary of the September 11 attacks Friday with a public remembrance at Hesky Park and the formal dedication of a new memorial garden at the town’s central fire station.

The town scheduled a procession from the Meredith Fire Department to Hesky Park before the noon ceremony. Police, firefighters and members of American Legion Griggs Wyatt Post 33 joined the observance, which honored the people killed in the attacks and the responders whose service followed.

After the service, participants were invited to march back to the fire station for the garden dedication. The town arranged overflow parking at the municipal lot on Route 3 and shuttle service beginning before the ceremony to help people reach both locations.

The two-part program connected a statewide day of remembrance to a permanent local site. By placing the memorial at the fire station, Meredith created a place where residents can return after the anniversary ceremonies end. The dedication also added another community memorial to the network of New Hampshire observances held Friday from Portsmouth to the Lakes Region.
dek: The Lakes Region community gathered at Hesky Park before a procession to the new memorial garden at the central fire station.
headline: Meredith dedicates September 11 memorial garden
